grammarChart.title: Passive Voice: be + Past Participle
grammarChart.structure: Subject + be (am, is, are, was, were, been, being) + Past Participle (V3)
grammarChart.purpose: To emphasize the action or the receiver of the action, rather than the doer.

tenses.active: Someone will have cleaned the room.
tenses.passive: The room will have been cleaned.

explanation: The passive voice is a grammatical construction where the subject of a sentence receives the action of the verb, rather than performing it. It is formed using a form of the verb 'to be' (am, is, are, was, were, been, being) followed by the past participle of the main verb.  We use the passive voice when the doer of the action is unknown, unimportant, or when we want to focus on the thing or person that is affected by the action.
keyRules: Identify the object of the active sentence. This becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
Use the correct form of the auxiliary verb 'to be' according to the tense of the active sentence.
Use the past participle (V3) of the main verb.
The original subject of the active sentence can be introduced with 'by' if it is important to mention.
Ensure subject-verb agreement in the passive sentence.
azarNotes: In formal writing, especially academic essays and reports, the passive voice is frequently used to maintain objectivity and focus on the research or findings rather than the researcher.
Be mindful of overusing the passive voice. Too much passive voice can make your writing sound indirect, wordy, and less engaging.

examples.active: The government introduced new policies last year.
examples.passive: New policies were introduced by the government last year.

examples.active: Scientists are conducting research on climate change.
examples.passive: Research on climate change is being conducted by scientists.

examples.active: The company will launch the product next month.
examples.passive: The product will be launched by the company next month.

examples.active: Students must submit their assignments by Friday.
examples.passive: Assignments must be submitted by students by Friday.

commonMistakes: Incorrect form of 'to be': Using 'is' instead of 'was' for past tense, or omitting 'be' altogether.
Incorrect past participle: Using the base form or simple past instead of the past participle (e.g., 'was write' instead of 'was written').
Confusing active and passive:  Using the passive structure when the subject is performing the action.
Tense errors:  Not matching the tense of 'to be' to the original active sentence.
ieltsTip: In IELTS Writing Task 1 (Academic), you will frequently use the passive voice to describe processes or data. For example, 'The raw materials are mixed...' or 'The figures were analyzed...'. In Task 2, use it judiciously to present arguments objectively or to discuss general truths.  Focus on clarity and accuracy.

quiz.question: Choose the correct passive form of the following sentence: 'The chef prepared a delicious meal.'
options: A delicious meal prepared the chef.
A delicious meal was prepared by the chef.
A delicious meal is prepared by the chef.
A delicious meal prepares the chef.

quiz.question: Identify the passive sentence:
options: The students are reading a book.
A book is being read by the students.
The students have read a book.
The students will read a book.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence with the correct passive form: 'The bridge _______ by engineers next year.'
options: will build
will be built
is built
was built

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses the passive voice to emphasize the object?
options: The artist painted the portrait.
The portrait was painted by the artist.
The artist is painting the portrait.
The portrait painted the artist.

quiz.question: Change the active sentence to passive: 'The committee has approved the proposal.'
options: The proposal has approved the committee.
The proposal is approved by the committee.
The proposal has been approved by the committee.
The committee has been approved by the proposal.
